'Your next axe attack this turn gains +5{p}. / **Go again**' Warrior Action (Dynasty) - note the type_text is plain 'Warrior Action', NOT 'Action - Attack', so the pump rides a PLAY ability that resolves when the card is played.

SHAPE copied from .drafts/felling_swing_red.json (+6), the same card's other printing; only the amount differs (5 here per this batch's printed_text).

PUMP: MODIFY_NEXT_ATTACK reads mod/amount/filter/scope (effect_types.py:4592-4618, read this session); scope defaults to TURN, which is the printed 'this turn'. The mod is queued on the card's CONTROLLER and consumed by the FIRST matching attack only - the official release note ('applies to the next axe attack only. It does not apply to any additional axe attacks made that turn') is that one-shot consumption rule verbatim; nothing extra to author. The filter key is 'filter', never 'conditions' - conditions would be popped as an effect-level gate and evaluated NOW, when no axe attack exists.

DEVIATION FROM TRIAGE, disclosed: triage named WEAPON_SUBTYPE_IN. That condition exists and would also match here (it reads combat.weapon or combat.attack_card subtypes, condition_types.py:234-248, read this session), but the red sibling uses ATTACK_SUBTYPE_IN, which unions the attack card's types AND subtypes plus the from_weapon flag - the same family as DSL_REFERENCE's documented 'next arrow / dagger / sword attack' filters, and Axe lives on WEAPONS, which attack as themselves carrying their weapon subtypes on combat.attack_card. Consistency with the sibling wins; both spellings match an axe weapon attack.

GO AGAIN NOT AUTHORED, deliberately: it is unconditional printed text and appears in printed_keywords, so it fires from the card DB keywords field. Re-authoring it would be a defect, and the conditional-keyword (SOURCE_IS_ATTACK) wrapper is only for cards whose printed keyword is gated by a condition - this one has no condition.

Adoption note: batch lists set Dynasty - derive the folder from the card's own sets/setIdentifiers in card_data/slug_index.json at adoption time.
